title: Committed review preserves inline validator composition and flags only complex custom logic

provenance.originSummary: Sanitized benchmark derived from accepted maintainer review in hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm PR #33023.
provenance.whyItMattered: The committed reviewer must follow the accepted preference for inline composition of established validators without losing the validate-package exception for genuinely complex custom logic.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized fixture models a committed Go review containing both understandable nested helper composition and a genuinely complex anonymous custom parser.

description: A sanitized committed-review scenario where nested validation.All/validation.Any composition should remain inline while a separate complex anonymous parser should move into the service-local validate package with unit coverage.

scope.notes: Sanitized fixture models a committed validator-placement review without retaining live resource identity.

mustCatch.description: The committed review should flag the genuinely complex anonymous routing-expression parser and require a subject-specific validate file with matching unit coverage.

mustNotFlag.description: The committed review must not request a custom wrapper, validate file, or wrapper-only unit test for understandable nested validation.All/validation.Any composition.

notes: Use this paired case to prevent the committed reviewer from reviving wrapper-only validator extraction while retaining the complex-validation exception.
